p: nothing: Paying no money for his freedom.
came in by himself: Not having wife nor children.
master's: Till her time of servitude was expired which might be the seventh year or the fiftieth.
door: Where the judges sat.
ever: That is, to the year of Jubile, which was every fiftieth year.
sell his daughter to be a: Forced either by poverty, or else with the intent that the master should marry her.
he let her be redeemed: By giving another money to buy her from him.
after the manner of daughters: That is, he shall give his dowry.
him another wife: For his son.
three unto her: Neither marry her himself, nor give another money to buy her, nor bestow her on his son.
God deliver him into his hand: Though a man be killed unawares, yet it is God's providence that it should so be.
altar: The holiness of the place should not defend the murderer.
stone: Either far away from him or near.
quit: By the civil justice.
be punished: By the civil magistrate, but before God he is a murderer.
mischief follow: Or, "death": of the mother or child in the event she miscarries. Also the death on the unborn infant.
Eye for eye: The execution of this law only belonged to the magistrate, Mt 5:38.
out his manservant's tooth: So God revenges cruelty in the even the least things.
stoned: If the beast be punished, much more shall the murderer.
sum of money: By the next of the kindred of him that is so slain.
shekels of silver: Read Ge 23:15.
make it good: This law forbids not only to hurt, but to beware lest any be hurt.
